content.title: About
content.content: Strawberries are edible berries of the plant Fragaria × ananassa, cultivated in temperate regions. The fruits are bright red, sweet‑tart, and juicy. Strawberries are eaten fresh, used in desserts, baked goods, smoothies, and jams.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Strawberries are one of the few berry plants whose seeds are also edible.
They contain more vitamin C than oranges by about 30 %.
There are over 600 strawberry varieties differing in size, aroma, and harvest time.
Strawberries are a symbol of spring and feature in many cultural celebrations.
The first cultivated strawberries appeared in Europe in the 18th century.

items.title: Rich in vitamin C
items.content: Vitamin C is a powerful antioxidant that supports immunity and collagen synthesis.

items.title: Contains antioxidants
items.content: Flavonoids such as anthocyanins help combat free radicals and reduce chronic disease risk.

items.title: Supports heart health
items.content: Strawberries provide potassium and dietary fiber, which help maintain normal blood pressure and cholesterol levels.

items.title: Aids blood sugar control
items.content: Low glycemic index and fiber slow sugar absorption.

items.title: Source of folate
items.content: Folate is essential for DNA synthesis and especially beneficial for pregnant women.

items.title: Allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to strawberries, such as skin itching or swelling.

items.title: Pesticide residues
items.content: Strawberries are often treated with pesticides; thorough washing or choosing organic berries is recommended.

items.title: Acidity
items.content: High acidity can irritate the stomach lining in people with gastritis or ulcers.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Strawberries can be eaten fresh, added to yogurt, cereals, salads, desserts, and smoothies. They can also be made into jam, sauce, or frozen for later use.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store strawberries in the refrigerator in their original container or a shallow bowl covered with plastic wrap. Use within 2–3 days. Do not wash until ready to eat to prevent spoilage.
